finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result, so there is no authorization check. Any caller can delete any account.
finding.source: Authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary id belonging to another user.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives a user-controlled id
Account is fetched by id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is discarded

finding.guards_checked: canDelete's result is unused. Unlike closeAccount, there is no assertCanDelete call and no throw. No other auth layer exists in the file.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9) returns a boolean but is called as a bare statement at line 22, so the result is discarded. The throwing variant assertCanDelete (line 13) is used only in closeAccount (line 29). No other auth layer or caller exists in the directory.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean result of canDelete is discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user on any account id. Unlike closeAccount (line 29), there is no throwing assertCanDelete call.
